correctness.rationale: Independent splitting proof: for X²=0 choose columns W lifting a reduced complement to ker(A), A=X mod π, and set U=XW. The columns (U,W) are independent mod π and extend to an R-basis. Take a coordinate map λ with λU=I and λW=0. Then P=Uλ+WλX is a projection onto the span of (U,W) and XP=PX=UλX. The complementary summand is free over the local ring and has residual X=0, since im(A) is contained in the reduction of the first summand. Its restriction is therefore π times a uniquely determined residue matrix B. This proves existence without a coefficient field. For uniqueness, on ker(A) a lift changes the divided image by a vector in im(A); a change of representative by Av is lifted by X applied to a lift of v and has zero further image. The divided image is in ker(A) by X²=0 and ann(π)=πR. This gives the k-linear, conjugacy-equivariant homology map, equal to B in the splitting. Conversely any similarity of B lifts to a change of complementary basis. A different generator uπ changes the homology label by the residue of u inverse. For each r, s=n−2r, the partitions indexed by monic irreducibles count B, giving the rational-canonical Euler product by unique factorization. Summing over r multiplies it by (1−z²)^{-1}; expansion through z³ gives q, q²+q+1, and q³+q²+2q. This also handles r=0, s=0 and residue characteristic two. The recorded finite checks are not needed for the proof and were not rerun.
residual_risks: The result counts conjugacy classes, not individual orbit sizes; no coefficient-field hypothesis or longer-ring analogue is inferred.

value.rationale: This classifies all free square-zero differentials up to isomorphism over the short local rings in scope. Residue rank and Smith data can coincide while the homology maps are nonsimilar: already X=πI_2 and X=π times a size-two Jordan block at eigenvalue 1 have the same Smith data and different classes. Giving the missing complete invariant and an all-dimension orbit series uniform in ring characteristic is structurally useful.
residual_risks: No finer classification such as centralizer sizes or applications to longer rings is required or inferred.
